solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dietary supplement that could make you go masculine

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the letters of the following words could be reworked to form something new

explanation.surface: A health-food advert warning that a supplement might make you more manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges the eleven letters of GO MASCULINE; 'you' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This amino sugar is sold as a supplement taken for joint health, so it is a dietary supplement by example.

clue.text: Cloth, not soft, put on the table

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is to be left out of the cloth

parts.note: plaid is a tartan woollen cloth
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Laying a tablecloth that is not soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes P from PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid has been set down or placed, as cutlery is put on a table.

clue.text: Sweets lose vitality in containers

indicators.note: in places the phrase before it inside the containers

parts.note: cans are tin containers
to die is to lose all life and vitality

explanation.surface: Confectionery going stale inside its jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweets' reads as a verb phrase subject, but it is the noun definition; 'in' is the container signal, with 'lose vitality' as the inner verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Candies is the American word for sweets, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Maybe something in the garden the woman had got rid of

definitions.meaning: a small outbuilding for tools, typically found in a garden
the contraction of she plus had, with the apostrophe ignored
past tense of a verb meaning to cast off or discard, as a snake its skin

explanation.surface: A woman clearing out something from her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three separate meanings of the same four letters, one needing the apostrophe of a contraction overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden outbuilding, a contraction meaning she had, and a past tense meaning discarded all share one spelling.

clue.text: Sheep knocked over barrier somewhere in Kent

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: A sheep has charged and flattened a farm gate in rural Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns RAM into MAR. MARGATE is a seaside town in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a seaside resort on the north Kent coast, so it is an example of a place in that county.

clue.text: Boy heading west in 28

indicators.note: in an across-style reading, heading west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the name Leon sits inside the answer to 28 across, between SIERRA and the final E

explanation.surface: A lad travelling west within an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: LEON is found in SIERRA LEONE (28 across); 'heading west' reverses it to give a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a male given name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Spot decrepit man wandering about

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters roam around and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A feeble old man is roaming about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering about' rearranges the letters of DECREPIT MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a spot is to be in a difficult situation, a tight corner or plight.

clue.text: A millionaire is so courageous

parts.note: the word millionaire has the big cat's name at its centre, so it is literally brave-hearted in that sense

explanation.surface: A rich person praised for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at the spelling: mil-LION-aire has LION at its heart, so the word is described as having a lion's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the heart of a lion means being exceptionally brave, so it is a synonym for courageous.

clue.text: Index woman uses maybe to find plant

parts.note: a woman's, written as lady's, the possessive showing what she uses
the index is the forefinger, an example of a finger

explanation.surface: A woman pointing her forefinger at a plant to identify it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the index as just one example of a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's finger is another name for okra, a vegetable plant with long slender pods.

clue.text: One traipsed around in misery

indicators.note: around here means the letters are moved round into another order

explanation.surface: A lonely figure trudging about in unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface of a lone walker trudging around hides the anagram signal 'around'; 'One' is fodder, not a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperation is a state of hopeless despair, close in sense to misery.

clue.text: Handyman should have his enthusiasm well-balanced

parts.note: spirit means energy, liveliness and enthusiasm
level means even and evenly balanced

explanation.surface: A good handyman needs a keen yet balanced temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a handyman's toolkit should contain this tool for checking surfaces are horizontal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble-in-a-tube gauge for checking horizontal surfaces is a standard tool any handyman should carry.

clue.text: Understood Socialist's pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a Red is a socialist or communist, from the red flag; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A socialist's speech was well understood.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of the verb meaning to interpret, rhyming with bed, sounds like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have read a situation or person is to have understood or interpreted them.

clue.text: Bound to find energy in drink

indicators.note: in places the letter for energy inside the drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Being sure to get a boost from an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but Bound is the definition, a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump or spring forward, the same as a leap.

clue.text: Doctor you repeatedly start to dread, not betraying emotions

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for you is given twice

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps telling a patient to face fear calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles YE; 'start to' takes the first letter of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dry-eyed sheds no tears, so shows no outward emotion.

clue.text: Money taken from bank account when old socialite gets with it

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young upper-class woman entering society, an old-fashioned term
taken as written

explanation.surface: A banking transaction made when a society girl goes shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: A DEB(utante) was a well-born young woman formally introduced into British high society; 'gets with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an entry recording a sum withdrawn from an account.

clue.text: Person unable to maintain momentum? One may get it in the neck

definitions.meaning: someone who comes to a halt, one who stops

definitions.text: One may get it in the neck
definitions.meaning: a cork or plug that is pushed into the neck of a bottle

explanation.surface: A flagging person who might get punished for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get it in the neck' suggests being punished, but it is literal: a bottle's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper is a plug for a bottle, and playfully also someone who stops.

clue.text: Tin revealed in the grass

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
something out is revealed or made public

explanation.surface: A tin can turns up in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' here is slang for a police informer, not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is British slang for a police informer, which is also called a grass.

clue.text: Net for flower

definitions.meaning: a large vertical fishing net weighted at the bottom
a crossword sense: something that flows, a river, here the one through Paris

explanation.surface: A net for catching a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a thing that flows, a river; this one runs through Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A seine is a fishing net, and the Seine is a French river, which is something that flows.

clue.text: Copper joining force with force supplying part of his equipment

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
F is the physics symbol for force
F again for the second force

explanation.surface: A police officer joins the force and is issued kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper first reads as a policeman, and 'his equipment' continues that picture: a cuff is part of a handcuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer carries handcuffs, colloquially cuffs, so one cuff is part of his kit.

clue.text: Animal losing tail isn't sweet

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter of the animal word is dropped

parts.note: a brute is a beast or animal

explanation.surface: A beast that has lost its tail is not cute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' removes the last letter E from BRUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine, the opposite of sweet.

clue.text: Get rid of disreputable person at Oxford?

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a rake or dissolute person
up means in residence at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Expelling a scoundrel from Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear up a document is to destroy it, so to discard or get rid of it.

clue.text: Ruddy grass upset wild animal!

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

explanation.surface: A red-faced person knocks over some grass while chasing a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REED to DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large wild deer of Europe and Asia, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Gift that is placed at end of drive

indicators.note: placed at end of puts the abbreviation after the other piece

parts.note: to press is to drive or push hard
ie, id est, is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A present left at the end of someone's driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like a driveway; it is the verb press.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressie is informal British slang for a present, which is a gift.

clue.text: Tower encountered across various parts of Iran

indicators.note: across here means the first piece stretches over the other, holding it inside

parts.note: met is the past of meet, meaning encountered

indicators.note: various parts suggests the pieces of the country name are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a tower in several regions of Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various parts of' jumbles the country into INAR; 'across' has the meeting word straddle it, the name in the surface being fodder rather than a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the tall slender tower of a mosque, a type of tower.

clue.text: Administrator needs support, having become dull inside

indicators.note: inside puts the dulling word within the support

parts.note: a tee is a peg supporting a golf ball
to rust is to corrode and lose shine, becoming dull

explanation.surface: An official needs backing after growing bored at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf tee is the support, split around the dulling word by 'inside'; 'needs' and 'having' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee administers property or funds held in trust for others.

clue.text: In the auditorium is aware of dissidents

indicators.note: an auditorium is where people listen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to know something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: An audience member senses the protesters in the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'noes' are those voting against in a parliamentary division, hence dissenters.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes are votes or voters against a motion, so they are the dissenting side.

clue.text: Garment is hairy, is missing odd bits

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters keeps the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A garment described as hairy has bits missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of IS HAIRY IS: s, a, r, i.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Flag when presented with a long account

parts.note: to flag is to tire and droop, to sag

explanation.surface: Someone growing weary while giving a lengthy story.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag reads as a banner, but here it is the verb meaning tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story or a lengthy, involved account.

clue.text: Poet has work displayed in gym

indicators.note: displayed in puts the work inside the gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A poet shows a new piece of work in the school gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander POPE was an English poet; PE is the British school subject of physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Portray endless suffering

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to paint is to portray or depict

explanation.surface: Depicting never-ending anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the T from PAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is physical or mental suffering, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Is Scot at back of beer parlour turning crude?

indicators.note: at back of places the earlier words after the beer
turning says the room is read round the other way

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a bar, a bar parlour, is a room in a pub
taken as written
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot in a pub's back room getting vulgar over his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the beer-and-parlour pair as one unit, not each word separately; 'at back of' puts the Scot and 'Is' after it. Ian is a stock Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelaisian means bawdy and coarse in humour, like the writing of Rabelais, so crude.

clue.text: Earlier ones travelling around country

indicators.note: travelling around has the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Early explorers journeying around a land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling around' is the anagram signal; the country is a fitting partner for the travelling picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a country in West Africa, an example of a country.
